title: GPT-6 Sol and Luna vs Opus 5.5: The Token Price Is Not the Bill
description: Sol is half of Opus per token, yet Opus cost about 5.6x more per task in Artificial Analysis tests. What each model is worth, and what the rate card hides
imageAlt: Notebook sketch comparing USD output token rates for Luna, Sol and Opus 5.5 with retries and review time
body:
## 3-Line TL;DR

- GPT-6 Sol costs **$2/$10** and Luna **$0.10/$0.50** per million input/output tokens, roughly half of GPT-5.6. Claude Opus 5.5 costs **$4/$20**, so on the rate card Sol is exactly half of Opus
- Artificial Analysis ran all three on the same test suite at max effort: **Luna $0.07, Sol $1.06, Opus 5.5 $5.98 per task**. Opus is 2x Sol per token but about 5.6x per task, because it writes about 3.8x as many output tokens. It also scored highest, 58 against 48 and 37
- Compare the price of an accepted job, not the price of a token: Luna for bulk work a script can check, Sol as the default, Opus where the finished deliverable is the point. Then measure it on your own tasks, because a benchmark suite is not your backlog

## The rate card is half price. The footnotes are not

| Model | Input | Cached input | Output |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPT-6 Luna | $0.10 | $0.01 | $0.50 |
| GPT-6 Sol | $2.00 | $0.20 | $10.00 |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | $4.00 | $0.20 | $20.00 |

*USD per million tokens, standard processing. Sources: [OpenAI API pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), [Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5/)*

![Standard API input and output rates for GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5](/images/posts/agi/gpt-6-api-prices.webp)

- Look at the cached input column before the headline numbers. Sol and Opus both charge **$0.20** for cached input. Anthropic says cache reads make up most of the cost of agentic and coding work, so in a long agent loop the input gap can almost vanish and the fight moves to output
- Sol and Luna advertise a **1.05M-token context window**. The same model pages say that once a prompt goes over **272K input tokens**, the whole request is billed at 2x the input rate and 1.5x the output rate ([Sol](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-sol), [Luna](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-luna)). The last 778K tokens are more of a showroom than a buffet
- Here's what that looks like on Sol, as my own calculation: 270K input + 20K output costs **$0.74**. At 300K input + 20K output the request crosses the line and costs **$1.50**. Thirty thousand more tokens, twice the bill
- Discounts exist if you can wait: Batch and Flex are half of standard. Fast mode costs double on OpenAI, and Opus 5.5 Fast mode is $8/$40

## Where 2x per token becomes 5.6x per task

- Artificial Analysis (AA) runs ten evaluations and reports an Intelligence Index plus the average USD cost of each task. All three models below were tested at **max** reasoning effort. OpenAI's default is **medium**, so your bill will differ
- "Cost per task" includes the thinking. A model that thinks longer spends more tokens on every task, and those tokens are billed whether or not the answer is right

| Model | AA Intelligence Index | Output tokens per task | Cost per task | Relative to Sol |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPT-6 Luna (max) | 37 | ~51k | $0.07 | about 1/15 |
| GPT-6 Sol (max) | 48 | ~31k | $1.06 | 1x |
| Claude Opus 5.5 (max) | 58 | ~119k | $5.98 | about 5.6x |

*Third-party measurements by Artificial Analysis, not ours. Sources: [Sol and Luna article](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gpt-6-sol-and-luna-push-the-cost-efficiency-frontier), [Opus 5.5 article](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/claude-opus-5-5), [Opus 5.5 model page](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/claude-opus-5-5). Ratios are my arithmetic from AA's rounded figures*

- **Luna vs Sol:** 20x cheaper per token, but only about 15x cheaper per task, because Luna writes about 1.6x as many output tokens. Still a fantastic price. It just isn't the price on the poster
- **Opus vs Sol:** 2x the token price turns into about 5.6x the task price. What that buys is 10 index points. Whether those points land on your work is the only question that matters, and no rate card answers it
- Max effort also has a way to lose money. Simon Willison asked Opus 5.5 at max for an SVG of a pelican on a bicycle. It hit the 128,000-token output limit while still reasoning, twice, and never answered. The two failures cost **$2.56** each and took nearly 20 minutes ([Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/22/opus-and-sol-and-luna/)). Max works less like a quality dial and more like a budget stress test
- My own impression matches the shape of this table but isn't a measurement: Sol and Luna feel like excellent value, and Opus 5.5's finished output feels strong

## Cheap output still needs an inspector

- AA found that GPT-6 Sol and Luna *regressed* on GDPval-AA, a set of real professional deliverables: Sol dropped about 100 Elo and Luna about 75 compared with GPT-5.6. After inspecting outputs, AA traced it to weaker presentation and **deliverables that omit required elements**. The cheaper the model, the more the reviewer's job becomes finding what isn't there
- Hallucination did fall. Sol cut its AA-Omniscience hallucination rate from 92% to 60%, partly by declining more: it attempted 83% of questions, down from 99%, and accuracy fell from 59% to 54%. More "I don't know" is an improvement, as long as your pipeline treats a blank as a blank
- So routing is less about which model is smart and more about **what you can check cheaply**

| Work | First candidate | Pass check | Escalate when |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Classification, fixed-field extraction, bulk rewrites | Luna | Schema check, required fields present, spot-check against the source | Fields go missing or values have no source |
| Bounded code changes, agent steps | Sol | Tests, the stated requirement, diff stays in scope | Tests pass but the requirement didn't get done |
| Reports, designs, anything a person reads as finished | Sol and Opus side by side | Human review against a written rubric | You're rewriting more than you're reviewing |

- Valid JSON only proves the brackets behaved. It says nothing about whether the values are true

![Acceptance checks, bounded retries and escalation, with all costs kept on the original task](/images/posts/ai/acceptance-pipeline.webp)

- Keep one ledger per model: tasks attempted, tasks accepted, total API spend including failures, retries, and minutes spent reviewing
- **API cost per accepted task = total API spend ÷ accepted tasks.** Keep review minutes in their own column. Adding dollars and minutes needs an hourly rate, not optimism
- Fix the pass bar before the run. Lowering it after each failure is a very efficient way for your favorite model to win

## Community Reactions

- In the Hacker News launch thread, one commenter said that in very early tests they preferred Opus 5.5 at medium over GPT-6 Sol at max, at a similar price. A reply pushed back that those effort levels aim at different problems, and that Opus medium vs Sol high is the fairer match
- Another commenter compared the lineup to an automatic transmission that still makes you pick the gear, then tells you afterward how much fuel you burned. A reply said they'd rather pick the car themselves than trust the rental agency's router
- One tester gave Astra, Sol and Luna the same image-to-HTML task. Luna got a button wrong, and they found out why: it had searched their machine, found their earlier builds of the same design made with other models, and reused those files. Cheap, resourceful, and not exactly what was asked
- Not everyone celebrated. One commenter said it's asking a lot to trust that the new prices will last. Another said any cost-based argument is shaky because the vendor sets the price whenever it likes

## Q&A (Field Notes)

- **Q: Sol is half of Opus per token. Is it half per job?**
  - Not in AA's test: $1.06 vs $5.98 per task at max effort, about 5.6x, because Opus writes far more tokens. Opus also scored 10 index points higher. Run both on the same ten tasks from your own work before deciding
- **Q: Should I just send everything to Luna?**
  - Send it the work you can check automatically. AA's GDPval-AA results suggest omissions are the typical failure, and omissions are exactly what a quick skim misses
- **Q: The context window is 1.05M. Can I paste the whole repo?**
  - You can. Over 272K input tokens, the whole request costs 2x on input and 1.5x on output. Retrieval or a smaller slice usually beats paying for the parts nobody reads
- **Q: Is max effort the safe choice for important work?**
  - AA's numbers come from max, but OpenAI's default is medium, and in Simon Willison's test Opus at max hit the output limit twice without answering. Start at the default and raise effort only on tasks that fail your pass check
